failures.title: Renault H5Ft Engine Problems - What Actually Fails

items.title: Timing Chain Stretch and Tensioner Wear - 2012-2018 models
items.whatHappens: The H5Ft's timing chain can stretch prematurely, particularly if oil change intervals are extended or incorrect oil specifications are used. This leads to a distinct rattling noise on cold starts and, in severe cases, chain skip or breakage, causing catastrophic valve-to-piston contact.
items.repairVsReplace: A standalone timing chain kit replacement costs £600-£1,200. However, if the chain has already skipped teeth and caused internal damage, a full Renault H5Ft engine replacement is the only viable option to restore reliability.

items.title: Turbocharger Wastegate Rattle and Oil Consumption - 60,000+ miles
items.whatHappens: The turbo wastegate actuator is prone to wear, causing a metallic rattling sound under acceleration and inconsistent boost pressure. Concurrently, some H5Ft units exhibit higher-than-normal oil consumption, which can starve the turbo of lubrication if not monitored closely between services.
items.repairVsReplace: Turbo replacement or actuator repair costs £500-£1,200. If oil starvation has caused turbo failure and sent metallic debris into the intake, a reconditioned unit is required to prevent recurring damage.

failures.goodYearsLine: Post-2015 revisions of the H5Ft received updated timing chain guides and revised ECU mapping to mitigate oil consumption, making these later units more robust, though strict oil change intervals remain critical .

variants.title: How to Confirm You Have the Renault H5Ft
variants.intro: The H5Ft engine code is stamped on a machined pad on the engine block, typically visible near the oil filter housing or on the timing cover. It is also clearly listed on your vehicle's V5C registration document under "Engine Capacity/Code" and can be verified via a VIN decode. Owners frequently confuse the H5Ft with the older, larger K4M (1.6 16v) or the newer H4Jt (1.3 TCe). While they share similar layouts, the H5Ft has specific ECU mappings, turbo plumbing, and fuel system fitments. Fitting the wrong revision can lead to sensor mismatches, incorrect fueling, and ECU faults. If your documentation shows K4M, view the K4M engine page. If it shows H4Jt, view the H4Jt engine page.

relatives.description: - The naturally aspirated 1.6-litre predecessor, lacking the turbo complexity but offering lower fuel efficiency and torque than the H5Ft.

- The higher-output 1.2 TCe variant; owners with the 130hp version should check this page for specific ECU and turbo differences before sourcing a replacement.

buyingGuide.title: Buying a Replacement Renault H5Ft - What to Choose

options.label: Used
options.body: A used Renault H5Ft engine is only advisable for low-value host vehicles and *only* if accompanied by documented proof that the timing chain and turbo were recently serviced. Without this, the risk of chain stretch or turbo failure is high.

options.label: Reconditioned
options.body: A proper reconditioned Renault H5Ft engine is the most recommended choice. It should include a new timing chain kit, updated tensioner, and a refurbished or new turbocharger. This addresses the engine's core weaknesses while keeping costs below a full rebuild.

options.label: Rebuilt
options.body: A full rebuild is justified for high-mileage examples or vehicles where the original block suffered catastrophic timing chain failure. An upgraded rebuild should feature reinforced chain guides and a revised oil pump to prevent future starvation.

buyingGuide.supplyFitLine: Sourcing and fitting through our vetted network ensures your new H5Ft is installed by specialists familiar with Renault's diagnostic requirements, backed by a minimum 12-month warranty and nationwide delivery.
buyingGuide.vehicleValueNote: For older hosts like the Megane Mk3 or Clio Mk4, current market values often sit between £2,500 and £7,000. Since a reconditioned Renault H5Ft supply-only starts around £1,400, the total fitted cost can approach or exceed 50% of the vehicle's value. In these cases, we strongly advise evaluating the scrap or part-exchange value before committing to a replacement.

items.question: How much does a Renault H5Ft engine replacement cost?
items.answer: A reconditioned Renault H5Ft engine costs between £1,400 and £2,500 for supply-only, with fitted costs typically ranging from £1,790 to £3,085. Used units start around £600 but carry a high risk of timing chain stretch. Rebuilt units with upgraded components range from £2,200 to £3,500.

items.question: What is the most common Renault H5Ft engine problem?
items.answer: The most documented failure is timing chain stretch and tensioner wear, typically occurring between 60,000 and 100,000 miles. Symptoms include a distinct rattling noise on cold starts and potential engine damage if the chain skips. If internal damage has occurred, a full Renault H5Ft engine replacement is the only viable option.

items.question: Should I buy a used or reconditioned Renault H5Ft?
items.answer: A reconditioned Renault H5Ft is strongly recommended over a used unit due to the known timing chain and turbocharger vulnerabilities. Reconditioned units should include a new timing chain kit, updated tensioner, and a refurbished turbocharger. A used engine is only viable if it has low mileage and verifiable proof of recent timing chain servicing.
